incumbent.name: Scott Alexander
incumbent.summary: Scott Alexander, a Muncie real estate appraiser and former Delaware County councilman, was first elected to the Senate in 2022 and is seeking a second term {caucus_alexander} {ipr_2022}. He serves on the Agriculture, Judiciary, Natural Resources, and Pensions and Labor committees {wfyi_guide26}.
record: Committees: Agriculture; Judiciary; Natural Resources; Pensions and Labor; interim study committees on government and pension management oversight, according to the Senate Republican caucus {caucus_alexander}.
April 15, 2025: Voted yes when the Senate gave final approval (27-22) to SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law {rc_sea1_417}.
April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the conference report for the 2025 state budget (HEA 1001), which passed the Senate 39-11 {rc_hb1001_538}.

Oct. 24, 2025: Announced he would support redrawing Indiana's congressional districts, saying "We cannot sit on the sidelines while the Democrats continue to gerrymander" {caucus_alexander_redistricting}. Dec. 11, 2025: Voted yes on HB 1032, the redistricting bill, which the Senate defeated 19-31 {rc_hb1032_8}. WFYI reported that day that Sen. Linda Rogers said Alexander had recently had open-heart surgery {wfyi_liveblog}.

2026 session: Authored SEA 144, which updates the state definition of tobacco to include vaping devices and raises the penalty for giving tobacco or e-liquid vaporizers to anyone under 21; it was ceremonially signed May 13, 2026. Alexander said such products "should never make it into the hands of minors" {caucus_alexander_sea144}.

2026 session: The caucus says Alexander supported SB 243, conforming state taxes to federal treatment of tips, overtime and auto-loan interest, and voted for HEA 1002 on utility affordability and reliability {caucus_alexander_2026}.

race_context: Senate District 26 covers all of Delaware and Randolph counties, including Muncie {wfyi_guide26}.

In 2022, after redistricting, Alexander won the seat with 61% of the vote over Democrat Melanie Wright, a former state representative {ipr_2022}. Wright now chairs Dale's campaign committee {dale_site}.
May 5, 2026 primaries: Alexander won the Republican nomination over Katherine (Kat) Nunley-Kritsch, and Andrew Dale was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {wlbc_primary}.

Key differences: Alexander voted for the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) {rc_sea1_417}, which Dale says should be repaired because it shifts the tax burden onto rural communities {dale_site}. Dale supports a 12-to-18-month moratorium on large data center development {wfyi_guide26}; no statement from Alexander on data centers was found. No debate or forum was found.

candidates.summary: Andrew Dale is a Muncie executive coach running as a Democrat {wfyi_guide26}. He focuses on affordability, public education funding, property-tax changes and rural health care {wfyi_guide26} {dale_site}.
background: Executive coach at Harbinger Coach, LLC; age 59; lives in Muncie {wfyi_guide26}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wlbc_primary}.

items: Calls for repairing SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, which he warns will harm rural communities through property-tax shifts {dale_site}.

Supports "a moratorium of 12 to 18 months on large data center development in Indiana" while environmental, zoning and public-health effects are studied {wfyi_guide26}; favors incentives for wind and solar over courting data centers {dale_site}.
Says utility costs are too high and the legislature should take a more active role in regulating them {wfyi_guide26} {dale_site}.

Wants a law barring unlawful dissolution of school corporations, citing Union School Corporation in Randolph County; opposes the voucher program; says "Keeping church out of school is a must" {dale_site}.
Wants rural hospitals and clinics protected from closure {wfyi_guide26} {dale_site}.
Calls for a comprehensive approach to housing, criticizes how Indiana handles tax-sale properties, and says homelessness should not be treated as a criminal matter {dale_site}.
Calls child care an economic issue that needs a lasting fix {dale_site}.
Proposes growing the education sector in Delaware County and supporting manufacturing, farmers and small businesses in both counties {dale_site}.

on_incumbent: No direct statements about Alexander or his record were found; Dale says he wants to be "a custodian of trust rather than a gatekeeper of possibilities" {wfyi_guide26}.
plans: Lists affordability, fully funded public education, state taxation and assessments, rural health care and preparing young people for the future as his priorities {wfyi_guide26}.
endorsements_finance: Top donors listed by WFYI from Transparency USA data are individuals, including Dale himself; no totals given {wfyi_guide26}.
gaps: Ballot Brief and Ballotpedia snippets say he holds degrees from Vincennes University and Ball State University and chairs the Delaware County Democratic Party; not confirmed from a primary source.
A Ball State Daily News profile was referenced by other sites but could not be located.
No endorsements or fundraising totals found.

candidates.summary: Scott Alexander is the incumbent, first elected in 2022, and owns a Muncie real estate appraisal firm {caucus_alexander} {wfyi_guide26}. His campaign lists jobs, roads, schools and responsive government as priorities {wfyi_guide26}.
background: Owner and operator of Alexander & Company Real Estate Appraisers; attended Delta High School, Vincennes University and Ball State University {caucus_alexander}.
Was a Delaware County councilman before his 2022 election {ipr_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Katherine (Kat) Nunley-Kritsch {wlbc_primary}.

items: Says more is needed so that Hoosiers "are not forced out of homes they own free and clear" over property-tax bills {caucus_alexander_afford}.
Says "Healthcare is too expensive" and backs legislation on cost transparency, prescription costs and hidden fees {caucus_alexander_afford}.
Backs letting employers offer child care as a benefit {caucus_alexander_afford}.
Supported mid-decade congressional redistricting in 2025, saying "The time to take action is now" {caucus_alexander_redistricting}.
Authored SEA 144 on tobacco and vaping products and minors {caucus_alexander_sea144}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements about Dale were found.
plans: Campaign priorities listed by WFYI: job protections, safe roads, dependable schools and responsive government {wfyi_guide26}.
endorsements_finance: Top donors listed by WFYI from Transparency USA data: Senate Majority Campaign Committee, Indiana Multi Family Housing PAC, Indiana Merit Construction PAC of ABC, Law PAC of Indiana and Indiana Realtors PAC; no totals given {wfyi_guide26}.
gaps: Did not respond to WFYI's 2026 survey; his campaign website could not be read.
Primary vote totals against Nunley-Kritsch were not found, nor what the primary campaign debated.
No endorsements or fundraising totals found.
